newsitem.title: FRANCE: French cabinet to study ambitious jobs programme.
newsitem.headline: French cabinet to study ambitious jobs programme.

text.p: The French cabinet will examine a bill on Wednesday to create 130,000 to 150,000 jobs for young people by the end of 1998, part of the Socialist-led government's drive to honour its electoral promises, employment ministry officials said on Tuesday.
The cabinet meeting will mark the first major government event of the "rentree", the traditional return to work and school after the summer holidays.

The cost of the jobs plan is calculated at between 11.9 billion ($1.9 billion) and 13.8 billion francs. But the employment drive will not affect the government's pledge to reduce France's public deficit to three percent of gross domestic product in 1998, to qualify for European monetary union, government officials have said.
The planned bill, seen as a priority by the government, will be debated by parliament at the start of an extraordinary parliamentary session slated for September 15.

The job creation effort will form part of the government's 1998 budget. Some two billion francs was unblocked in advance this year to create 30,000 to 50,000 jobs in 1997 and 100,000 will be created in 1998, employment ministry officials say.

During the election campaign, the Socialists promised to create 700,000 jobs, half in the public sector, half in the private sector. They said the job creation programme would be implemented over the normal five-year life of the government.
The money allocated for the job creation programme, set at 92,000 francs per post per year, will be on top of existing employment programmes costing an estimated 130 billion francs.
French unemployment stands at a record 12.6 percent or 3.1 million. Of that, some 583,000 jobless are under the age of 25.

Employment Minister Martine Aubry, number two in the government, said last week that she had been granted 10 billion francs to create 100,000 jobs and that this jobs initiative would not have an impact on existing programmes.
The youth job creation programme will target mainly those who have no training.
Each young person will receive a five-year contract, renewable each year, and the jobs will be intended to be "meaningful", according to the employment ministry.
The aim is to allow young people to become "professionals" and the ministry is looking at granting diplomas to those who participate, officials say.
After launching the public sector job programme, the government will seek to carry through with the other leg of its other electoral promise -- creation of 350,000 youth jobs in the private sector.
That goal will be on the agenda at a meeting at the end of September bringing together the government, employers and unions. ($ = 6.182 French Francs)
